purpose: Verify that the LibreOffice conversion path recalculates formulas before saving, so cached values written into the converted XLSX are correct for calamine consumers (PT-1-1/1-2/1-3 read caches only and never calculate).
why_this_matters: calamine only reads <v> cached values; the fullCalcOnLoad workbook flag is an Excel/WPS open-time hint that calamine ignores. Without an actual recalculation during conversion the downstream features would read stale numbers.

fixture.corruption_method: rewrite <v> of the formula cell inside xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml after openpyxl save, then rezip; this simulates a stale cache from a producer that never calculated

method.step_1: build the fixture with a stale cached value of 999
method.step_2: create an isolated LibreOffice profile and pre-seed user/registrymodifications.xcu with /org.openoffice.Office.Calc/Formula/Load OOXMLRecalcMode=0 (always recalculate)
method.step_3: run headless soffice --convert-to 'xlsx:Calc MS Excel 2007 XML' with -env:UserInstallation pointing at that profile
method.step_4: read the converted workbook with openpyxl data_only=True (same XML level calamine uses)

conclusion: With OOXMLRecalcMode=0 pre-seeded in the isolated profile, LibreOffice recalculates on load and SaveAs writes the recalculated value into the formula cache. The converted XLSX therefore carries trustworthy numbers for calamine readers.

implementation_reference.applied_at: libreoffice_user_installation_arg (every isolated profile created by the conversion runtime)

other_engines.com: Rust COM calls CalculateFullRebuild before SaveAs (pytools-core/src/conversion_com.rs)
other_engines.native: explicitly value-only: writes formula text without computing caches; not suitable for calamine cache consumers

scope_limits: This verifies the LibreOffice recalculation switch only; it does not re-run the full PT-4-2 conversion matrix on this image.
Final acceptance on Kylin V10 / UOS V20 still belongs to the project acceptance stage on the real target machines.
The Excel/WPS COM path was verified separately on Windows with a real formula workbook (cached result 27 = 10*2+7) and is covered by an automated regression test.
